paragraphs: Here's what I love about this psalm, friend. David doesn't pretend everything is fine. He says it plain: “Rescue me, O LORD, from evil men.” Then he takes the whole mess, the venom, the hidden traps, the people closing in, and brings it to the LORD instead of carrying it alone (Psalm 140:1, 3, 5).

Notice what he does in the middle of it. Right when the traps are set, he says to the LORD, “You are my God.” He calls Him “the strength of my salvation” and says, “You shield my head in the day of battle” (Psalm 140:6-7). David is going through it, and he's still holding on to WHO he's praying to. The trouble didn't get the last word, because he took it to God first.

Then the prayer turns. David stops asking and says, “I know that the LORD upholds justice for the poor and defends the cause of the needy” (Psalm 140:12). He ends sure that “the righteous will praise Your name; the upright will dwell in Your presence” (Psalm 140:13). So when somebody's working against you, baker, you can pray it all out loud, honest and messy. I've been shoved in the back of a drawer, so trust me on this: you can bring your trouble to the LORD and still end up knowing who He is.
